## What this is

**PLAN-0104 Step 7** — the gated live evidence run on MS-S1, executed under a **typed Cray §8 go requested for Step 7 by name (s228)**. This closes **AC-7**, the one claim no fixture can settle, and completes the PLAN **8/8**.

One warm + one sweep, per CLAUDE.md §8's minimize-live-runs rule. No other host state was touched.

## Step 7's four pre-committed reads — all PASS

The pass/fail was fixed **in the PLAN before the run** and is read from there, never restated.

| # | clause | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Emission (AC-7-i) | ✅ nl-13 → `operation:"count"` **with** `group_by:"asset_id"`, emitted on the **first pass** |
| 2 | Scoring (AC-7-ii) | ✅ `correct` under the exact, tolerance-free groups scorer; groups **relabelled to display names** — 5 / 3 / 3 / 2 = 13 |
| 3 | Re-measurement (AC-7-ii) | ✅ 13 cases: **12/13**, expressible 92%, ceiling-rescue 100%, p50 15.9s / p95 75.7s |
| 4 | No fixture re-recorded / no A/B re-run | ✅ `nl_query_ab_fixtures.py` diff empty |

## Evidence integrity — checked BEFORE spending the run

`CaseResult.query_json` comes from `ans.query`, which passes through the post-translate rewrite seam. Had `_infer_group_by` been able to synthesize a `group_by`, the artifact would have proved the **engine guessed it**, not that the **model emitted it** — which is the entire content of AC-7. `nl_query.py:971` early-returns unless `operation` is `max`/`min`, so it cannot fire on a `count` case.

The `goal-evaluator` independently corroborated this by a route I had not used: `:979` is the **only** site in the module that ever writes `group_by`, and `limit` varies across count cases (nl-02 → 1, nl-13 → 100), which a canned JSON would not.

## 🔴 The prior figure is RETIRED, not overwritten — and the obvious citation is a trap

`RESULTS.md:116`'s **`11/12` is the text-to-SQL arm**; the engine-A figure on that line is `8/12`. The prior **engine-A** accuracy is AC-9's `11/12` at **`RESULTS.md:316`** (2026-06-16, session 62). The two coincidentally share a number — which is precisely how the wrong one gets retired.

The record states both figures, the full lineage (`8/12 → 10/12 → 11/12 → [prompt + gold change] → 12/13`), **two independent sufficient reasons** (the shared system prompt changed in #1149; the gold set grew 12 → 13), an explicit *"must not be cited as an improvement"*, and a reading note disambiguating the arms. The original line is left intact.

## The lone miss (nl-06) — investigated before merge, per clause 3

nl-06 was correct in the prior recorded run, so the clause's single re-run applied. **It failed again**, which the clause makes *"a defect investigated before merge, not noise."*

**Finding: not a PLAN-0104 regression.**

- Failure shape is the catalogued whole-table filter-omission (`filters:[]` → all 4 assets), in this file since the 2026-06-14 spike
- #1149's diff changes **only the OPERATION sentence** — the FILTERS sentence is **byte-identical**
- The class is recorded as run-to-run variance and **the victim moved**: AC-9's lone miss was nl-01, which is **correct in this run**
- Both remedies are **proven negative** on this axis: 4 model families, 3 prompt variants, 5+ live runs
- Answer-correct, zero fabrication

**The one alternative a single sweep cannot refute to zero is recorded rather than smoothed over** — that the lengthened OPERATION sentence mildly dilutes attention to the FILTERS sentence — with its reopen condition stated in place: a future sweep showing simple-list filter-omission **concentrating** rather than **moving**.

## Bookkeeping correction, surfaced rather than silently fixed

`STATUS.md:115` asserts *"AC-1..AC-6 and AC-8 are CLOSED"*, but **every AC checkbox in the PLAN was still `[ ]` on disk** — the work shipped in #1145/#1148/#1149 and the closure was recorded only in STATUS. All eight are now ticked.

To be explicit about the basis: **AC-1..AC-6 and AC-8 are ticked against those merged PRs' recorded gate runs plus this PR's own full gate — not a fresh per-AC re-derivation.** AC-7 is closed by this run's evidence.

## Gates

Captured **after committing, before pushing**:

- full `tests/` — **4045 passed, 8 skipped**
- `mypy --strict services/` — clean over **134** source files
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` — clean, **judged on the HEAD tree** (`git archive HEAD`), because a bare run in the working dir also lints the untracked `.claude/benchmark-results/` and reports an S108 that is not in the repo

## Not in this PR, deliberately

Archiving PLAN-0104 to `docs/plans/done/` — the move requires retargeting every tracked reference in the same commit (R8), which belongs with the STATUS reconcile.

Refs: PLAN-0104 Step 7 + AC-7; CLAUDE.md §8; #1145 / #1148 / #1149.

+
+---
+
+## Addendum — PLAN-0104 Step 7 live evidence run (2026-08-13, session 228)
+
+The gated live confirmation for **AC-7** — the one claim no fixture can settle:
+whether the LIVE model emits `count` **together with** `group_by` now that
+PLAN-0104 Steps 1–6 taught the engine the pair and #1149 inverted the prompt's
+blanket *"never list/count"* rule. Run under a **typed Cray §8 go, requested for
+Step 7 by name (s228)** — one warm + one sweep, per CLAUDE.md §8's minimize-live-runs
+rule. `gpt-oss:20b` @ MS-S1 (`192.168.1.133:11434`), the shipped engine-A path
+(`run_benchmark.py` → `answer_question`) over the deterministic energy synthetic
+data. Dumps: `.claude/benchmark-results/s228-plan0104-step7.jsonl` and
+`…-step7-nl06-rerun.jsonl` — ⚠️ **untracked, NOT gitignored.** No `.gitignore`
+pattern matches `.claude/benchmark-results/`; `git status` reports it `??`. So
+the raw per-case evidence lives only in the working tree, is preserved nowhere
+in history, and is not protected against an accidental commit either. *(Earlier
+addenda in this file call their own dumps "gitignored" — same inherited error,
+left in place rather than rewritten across sections; this note is the
+correction.)* **Pass/fail was fixed in the PLAN before the run**
+(`docs/plans/0104-*.md` §Step 7); this records the reads against it.
+
+**Result: 12/13 correct · expressible 92% · ceiling-rescue 100% · lone miss nl-06
+· latency p50 15.9 s / p95 75.7 s / max 75.7 s.**
+
+### 🔴 The prior figure is RETIRED as non-comparable — it is not overwritten
+
+| | figure | status |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Prior** (AC-9, 2026-06-16, session 62 — this file, line ~316) | **11/12 correct** | 🔴 **RETIRED — non-comparable** |
+| **This run** (Step 7, 2026-08-13, session 228) | **12/13 correct** | current |
+
+**Two independent reasons, either one sufficient:** (1) the **shared system prompt
+changed** in #1149 — every engine-A accuracy recorded before it was produced under
+a different translate instruction; (2) the **gold set grew 12 → 13 cases** (nl-13,
+Step 5). The two numbers therefore measure different things and **must not be
+cited as a 11/12 → 12/13 improvement.** Both are stated here so the lineage stays
+readable: 8/12 (spike) → 10/12 (AC-8) → 11/12 (AC-9) → *[prompt + gold change]* →
+12/13 (Step 7).
+
+⚠️ **Reading note for anyone citing this file:** the `11/12` in the comparison
+table above (line ~116) is the **text-to-SQL arm**, a different architecture — it
+coincidentally shares the number with AC-9's engine-A figure. The engine-A lineage
+is the one listed above.
+
+### AC-7, clause by clause (the PLAN's own pre-committed reads)
+
+1. **Emission (AC-7-i) — PASS.** nl-13's recorded translate output:
+   `{"object_type":"OperationalEvent","operation":"count","filters":[],`
+   `"aggregate_property":null,"group_by":"asset_id",…}`. The pair is emitted by
+   the model on the first pass — no retry-loop recovery was needed (which the
+   clause would also have allowed). **Evidence integrity checked BEFORE the run:**
+   `_infer_group_by` (`services/engine/nl_query.py:971`) early-returns unless
+   `operation` is `max`/`min`, so a `group_by` on a `count` case **cannot** have
+   been synthesized by the deterministic rewrite seam — the value is the model's.
+2. **Scoring (AC-7-ii) — PASS.** nl-13 scores `correct` under the Step-5 scorer,
+   whose `groups` check is exact and tolerance-free. The per-group figures came
+   back **relabelled to display names** — Battery Bank A 5, Inverter Unit A 3,
+   Battery Bank B 3, Feeder Meter A 2 = **13** — matching the hand-verified gold;
+   an un-relabelled key or a collapsed bucket would have scored `wrong`.
+3. **Re-measurement (AC-7-ii) — PASS.** All 13 cases run; per-case outcomes in the
+   dump, headline above, prior figure retired as set out.
+4. **No fixture re-recorded, no A/B re-run — HELD.** `nl_query_ab_fixtures.py`
+   diff empty.
+
+### The lone miss (nl-06) — investigated before merge, per clause 3
+
+nl-06 (*"Show the asset named Battery Bank A."*) was **correct in the prior
+recorded run**, so clause 3's re-run applied: it was **re-run once and failed
+again**, which the clause makes *"a defect investigated before merge, not noise."*
+The investigation's finding is that it is **not a PLAN-0104 regression**:
+
+- **Failure shape:** the model emitted `Asset` with `filters:[]` → all 4 assets
+  (structured wrong vs gold 1). This is **Finding 1's whole-table filter-omission**,
+  catalogued in this file since the 2026-06-14 spike.
+- **The prompt edit does not touch it.** #1149's diff changes **only the OPERATION
+  sentence**; the FILTERS sentence (*"ALWAYS include the filter the question
+  implies — never return a whole-type read…"*) is **byte-identical** across the
+  commit.
+- **The class is documented as run-to-run variance, and the victim moved.** AC-9's
+  lone miss was **nl-01** by the same mechanism, described there as *"run-to-run LLM
+  variance on a simple list"* (the spike's nl-01 was wrong; AC-8 got it right; AC-9
+  wrong again). **In this run nl-01 is correct and nl-06 is not** — a moving victim
+  within a known-flaky class, not a systematic prompt regression.
+- **Both remedies are already PROVEN NEGATIVE** on this axis (2026-06-15 addendum):
+  4 model families all dropped implied filters; 3 prompt variants failed or
+  regressed, over 5+ live runs.
+- **Answer-correct, zero fabrication.** The phrase answer named exactly Battery
+  Bank A with its real rating, site and install date — the miss is an over-broad
+  *set*, never an invented fact.
+
+**Honest limit, recorded rather than smoothed over:** a single sweep cannot fully
+separate "known variance" from "the lengthened OPERATION sentence mildly diluting
+attention to the FILTERS sentence." The four points above make the variance reading
+much better supported — in particular the unchanged FILTERS text and nl-01 flipping
+*to* correct — but the alternative is not refuted to zero by this run alone. If a
+future sweep shows simple-list filter-omission concentrating rather than moving,
+that is the signal to reopen it.
+
+### Anti-hallucination — HELD
+
+Every answer cites only real values. nl-12 (*"list all open alerts"*, no Alert
+data) returned the deterministic *"No Alert records match that query."*
+(`grounded=false`). The nl-06 miss is an over-broad set narrowed correctly by the
+phrase step. **No fabrication anywhere.**
+
+**Verdict: AC-7 PASS** — the live model emits `count` + `group_by`, the case scores
+`correct` on the exact grouped-count scorer, and the full 13-case set is
+re-measured with the prior figure retired as non-comparable. This run is
+**evidence, not a gate** (CLAUDE.md §8): the offline oracle remains the gate.
+
+*AI-assisted (Claude Code, session 228); no `Co-Authored-By` per CLAUDE.md §7.*

details.body:
## Summary

Updates the `wow-look-at-my/dats` composite action so that on Linux it ensures bubblewrap sandboxing actually works before running tests. It installs `bubblewrap` if missing and clears Ubuntu 24.04's default `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns` restriction when it blocks bwrap, matching the approach already used in this repo's own CI.

The final bwrap check has no fallback: a runner where sandboxing genuinely cannot work fails loudly rather than silently shipping unsandboxed test runs. The step is skipped on non-Linux (macOS uses seatbelt, which needs no such fix).

Also updates `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to document the new behavior and removes the `--no-sandbox` workaround from the example usage.

## Test notes

- The sysctl write is wrapped in `|| true` so it acts as a harmless probe on kernels without the knob; the authoritative pass/fail signal is the final bwrap re-check.
- No test results are reported here; the change relies on the same `sudo sysctl` approach already proven in this repo's CI workflow.

### Claude sessions

- https://claude.ai/code/session_01JXwuTPBdcSRVkvKAD7TA3E

diff --git a/action.yml b/action.yml
index 5123a83..8a77635 100644
--- a/action.yml
+++ b/action.yml
@@ -31,6 +31,34 @@ runs:
         project: dats
         version: ${{ inputs.version }}
 
+    # dats sandboxes test commands by default (bubblewrap on Linux, seatbelt on
+    # macOS, docker otherwise) -- real isolation, not a formality, so a caller
+    # should never have to reach for --no-sandbox just to work around
+    # infrastructure. Skips on non-Linux (macOS's seatbelt sandbox needs
+    # neither of these steps).
+    - name: Install bubblewrap (Linux)
+      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
+      shell: bash
+      run: command -v bwrap >/dev/null 2>&1 || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap)
+
+    # Ubuntu 24.04 ships a default AppArmor restriction
+    # (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1) that silently denies
+    # bwrap's unprivileged user namespace even once it's installed; this
+    # repo's own CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) already proved sudo can clear
+    # it. The final bwrap check has no fallback -- a runner where this
+    # genuinely doesn't work should fail loudly here, not silently ship
+    # unsandboxed test runs.
+    - name: Configure bubblewrap so it actually works (Linux)
+      if: runner.os == 'Linux'
+      shell: bash
+      run: |
+        # The sysctl write can itself fail harmlessly (e.g. a kernel with no
+        # such knob) -- `|| true` keeps this a probe, not an abort, so the
+        # bwrap re-check below stays the one authoritative pass/fail signal.
+        bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp --unshare-pid --die-with-parent true \
+          || sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 || true
+        bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp --unshare-pid --die-with-parent true
+
     - name: Run dats
       shell: bash
       working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
